name: RRB ALP
fullName: Railway Recruitment Boards – Assistant Loco Pilot Recruitment
frequency: Annual (as per RRB calendar, usually notified in Jan–May)
approxCandidates: ≈8.4 lakh registrations reported for CEN 01/2026 (earlier cycles drew 18 lakh+)
eligibility: 10th pass + ITI/Course Completed Act Apprenticeship in notified trades, or Diploma/Degree in Mechanical/Electrical/Electronics/Automobile Engineering; 18–30 yrs (relaxation as per rules)

notification.summary: CEN 01/2026 notified 11,127 Assistant Loco Pilot vacancies; online applications ran from 15 May to 14 June 2026. As per the RRB schedule notice of 21 Sep 2026, CBT 1 is tentatively scheduled for 3, 4 and 5 November 2026, with city intimation slips about 10 days and e-call letters about 4 days before each candidate's exam date.

pattern.notes: CBT 1 is a screening test: marks are not counted for the final merit list; candidates are shortlisted for CBT 2 (Part A 100 Q + qualifying trade Part B 75 Q) by normalised CBT 1 score. 1/3 negative marking. Qualifying percentage: UR/EWS 40%, OBC/SC 30%, ST 25%. CBAT (psycho test) and DV/Medical (A-1 standard) follow.

trendAnalysis.summary: ALP CBT 1 papers (CEN 01/2024 in Nov 2024, CEN 01/2025 in early 2026) were moderate with tight time – 75 questions in 60 minutes. Mathematics is calculation-heavy (simplification, mensuration, time-work/pipes, SI/CI, algebraic identities). Reasoning carries the most marks with series, coding, blood-relation codes, syllogism and data sufficiency; it is slightly tougher than Group D. General Science is NCERT Class 9–10 based with a noticeable share of physics numericals (motion, electricity, optics). GA is only 10 questions, mostly science-tech, sports and government current affairs. Good attempts are typically 55–62 out of 75.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the two latest ALP CBT 1 cycles: CEN 01/2024 (CBT 1 held 25–29 Nov 2024) and CEN 01/2025 (CBT 1 held Feb 2026; no ALP CBT 1 was held in 2025 – that year had only the CEN 01/2024 CBT 2). RRB bars sharing of live questions, so web searches (Oct 2026) returned only shift-wise analyses (PracticeMock, Physics Wallah, Careers360) listing topic counts – e.g. SI 2–3, percentage 2–3, coding, series, blood relations, direction and two puzzle sets per shift. Question TYPES were described from those lists and the writer's own knowledge of released ALP/Group D/Technician papers (the CBT 1 syllabus is common); WebFetch of papers was not possible. All patterns are paraphrased.

archetypes.pattern: Divisibility test – which of four large numbers is divisible by 8/9/11, or find the missing digit that makes a number divisible
Remainder and unit-digit of large powers or products (cyclicity of 2, 3, 7, 8)
Primes and factors (identify the prime, count factors, sum of primes in a range) and sums of first n natural/odd/even numbers
Simplify an expression with "of", brackets and mixed operations; distractors from left-to-right evaluation that ignores "of"
Square roots/cube roots of perfect squares and decimals combined with basic operations
Compare/order fractions or add mixed fractions and decimals; convert recurring decimals to fractions
HCF/LCM of given numbers or fractions, and HCF × LCM = product of two numbers
Least/greatest number leaving the same remainder, bells tolling together – LCM/HCF word problems
Divide an amount in a given (or fractional) ratio; combine A:B and B:C into A:B:C
Present/future ages in a ratio, or a number added to both terms changes the ratio
Successive increase/decrease, net % change, "by what % is B less than A" reversal
Marks/elections/population growth word problems with percentages
2-D figures: area/perimeter of triangle (Heron), square, rectangle, circle from given data
3-D solids: volume/surface area of cube, cylinder, cone, sphere and melting–recasting
Two/three workers with individual or pair rates – time together, or time for one alone
Men–days–hours (M₁D₁H₁ = M₂D₂H₂) and efficiency comparison
Train crossing a pole/platform/another train (relative speed, km/h ↔ m/s)
Average speed for equal distances, speed unit conversion, boats and streams
Simple interest: find SI, rate or time; sum becoming k times itself
Compound interest for 2–3 years (annual/half-yearly) and CI − SI difference
Profit/loss % from CP and SP, SP needed for a target gain, false weights
Marked price with one or two successive discounts; mark-up then discount profit %
Algebraic identities: given a + b and ab (or x + 1/x) find a² + b², a³ + b³ etc.
Triangle angle properties (angle sum, ratio of angles, angle between bisectors, exterior angle)
Standard trigonometric values and identities (sin²θ + cos²θ, tan θ from a given ratio)
Mean/median/mode of a small data set; mean after adding or removing an observation

archetypes.topic: Square Root, Age, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
archetypes.pattern: Mixed short problems: pipes filling/emptying, age sums, odd days in calendar, angle between clock hands

Word-pair analogy: identify the relation in the first pair (instrument–quantity measured, worker–tool/workplace, organ–function, product–raw material) and pick the term that completes the second pair; distractors share the category but not the relation

Number or letter-cluster analogy: first pair linked by n² ± k, n³, n(n+1) or a fixed letter shift; apply the same rule to the third term; distractors come from the neighbouring rule (n² vs n²+1, etc.)
Number series – find the next/missing term; rules are increasing differences, ×n ± k, squares/cubes or primes; distractors are values from applying the rule with an off-by-one step
Letter or letter-cluster series: each letter in a cluster moves by a fixed/increasing step (+2, +3 …) or skips letters; choose the next cluster; distractors miss one letter shift
Letter-shift coding: a word is coded by shifting each letter (+k, alternating ±k, position-based shift or reverse + shift); find the code of a new word or decode a code
Number/position coding: word coded as sum or product of alphabet positions or reverse positions, or common-word sentence codes; find the code of a new word
Symbol substitution: + − × ÷ (or letters) are re-defined; substitute and evaluate with BODMAS; distractors come from left-to-right evaluation
Interchange two signs (or numbers) to make an equation correct, or find the hidden rule of a defined operation (e.g. a # b = a² + b²) and apply it
Pointing/introduction statement (e.g. "only son of my father's …") – decode the chain to name the relation; gender trap built into distractors
Coded relations (A + B means A is mother of B …) or a family chain of 4–6 people – find how X is related to Y or which expression is true
Two or three categorical statements (All/Some/No) followed by two conclusions; pick Only I / Only II / Both / Neither; traps are reverse "All" conversions and possibility cases
Arrange 4–5 words in dictionary order (or a logical/meaningful sequence) and report the word at a given position or the correct order
Choose the Venn relationship (disjoint, one inside another, partial overlap) that best represents three given classes
Two-set counting: totals, "both" and "neither" figures given – find only-A / neither / both
Data sufficiency: a question with Statement I and II – decide whether I alone, II alone, either, both together or neither is sufficient
Short everyday statement (railway/civic/public notice) with two conclusions or courses of action – select which logically follow
Odd one out among four words from a common category (planets, units, instruments, organs) where one breaks the property
Odd number / number-pair / letter-cluster out: three follow a numeric rule (prime, n:n², fixed gap) and one does not
Linear row of 5–7 people facing north/south with immediate-left/right and "between" clues – find who sits at a position or between two people
Ranking/comparison: position from both ends of a row/class, or ordering by height/weight/marks from comparative statements
Circular table seating (facing centre) or day/floor scheduling with 5–6 entities – identify neighbour/position
Walk path with left/right turns and distances – find the shortest distance and direction from the start (Pythagoras triples)
Facing direction after a series of clockwise/anticlockwise turns, or shadow-based direction at sunrise/sunset
Statement (notice/advertisement/advice) with two assumptions – decide which are implicit
Should-type policy statement with Yes/No arguments – decide which arguments are strong
Mirror/water image of a letter–number string or clock time, or counting triangles/squares in a simple figure

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: Equations of motion numericals (v = u + at, s = ut + ½at², v² = u² + 2as, free fall with g = 10 m/s²); distractors from forgetting ½ or using wrong sign

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: SI units, scalar vs vector, and Newton's laws concepts (inertia, action–reaction examples)

archetypes.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
archetypes.pattern: Momentum / F = ma / impulse numericals with unit conversion (g → kg, km/h → m/s)
Work, kinetic/potential energy and power numericals (W = Fs, KE = ½mv², PE = mgh, P = W/t) including "velocity doubled → KE ×4" type
Gravitation: universal law (effect of changing distance/mass), g on Moon, mass vs weight, free fall
Mirror/lens formula numericals: image distance, magnification, R = 2f; sign-convention traps in options
Refraction: refractive index and speed of light, power of lens P = 1/f (in metres), lens type from sign
Natural optical phenomena (scattering, total internal reflection, dispersion, twinkling) and defects of vision with correcting lens
Ohm's law and series/parallel resistance combinations – find equivalent resistance or current
Electric power and energy: P = VI = V²/R, kWh consumption and cost, heating effect (H = I²Rt)
Magnetic effects: Fleming's rules, right-hand thumb rule, motor vs generator, field lines, fuse/earthing
Wave numericals: v = fλ, time period, echo distance (2d = vt)
Properties of sound (audible range, infrasonic/ultrasonic, speed in media) and heat/temperature scale conversions
Atomic structure: protons/neutrons/electrons from Z and A, electronic configuration (K, L, M), valency, isotopes/isobars
Periodic table: group/period of an element from its configuration, trends in atomic size/metallic character, Döbereiner/Newlands/Mendeleev facts
Mole concept and molecular mass; states of matter, sublimation/evaporation concepts
Common salts – chemical formula/name/use of baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder, Plaster of Paris, gypsum
pH scale and indicators (litmus, phenolphthalein, methyl orange), neutralisation and everyday acids
Metals: reactivity series & displacement, ores and extraction, alloys and their constituents, corrosion/rancidity
Carbon compounds: homologous series formula (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ etc.), functional groups, IUPAC names, allotropes of carbon
Identify the type of reaction (combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox) from an equation
Oxidation–reduction: substance oxidised/reduced, oxidising agent; balancing coefficients
Diseases and their causative agents, vaccines, vitamin/mineral deficiency diseases
Human organ systems: digestive enzymes and organs, blood components, heart chambers, nervous system/brain parts, hormones
Plant life processes: photosynthesis requirements, xylem/phloem, transpiration, plant hormones and their functions
Mendel's monohybrid/dihybrid ratios, sex determination, evolution terms (homologous/analogous organs), food chains and ozone
ISRO and international space missions of the last 1–2 years – purpose, launch vehicle or partner agency
Indian astronauts/scientists in the news and indigenous technology or defence systems
Recent tournament results – winner/runner-up/host of cricket, hockey, football and multi-sport events
Individual players and records in chess, athletics, badminton, shooting, and sports awards
Personalities and their contributions – authors of national symbols, award-winning artists, reformers
Dances, festivals and monuments matched with states/dynasties
Government schemes/initiatives – launch year, ministry, objective or headline benefit
Economic institutions and terms – RBI, GST, budget, banking
Constitutional posts – who appoints/elects, current holders, oath and tenure
Constitutional Articles, amendments and parliamentary procedure
Indian Railways history, production units, zones and landmark bridges/trains
Freedom-struggle events and physical geography of India (rivers, passes, parks)
Awards (names, renaming, first recipients), books–authors, important days

resources.notes: RRBs publish the question paper, provisional answer key and response sheet for each ALP CBT only during the objection window, through regional RRB websites (e.g. https://www.rrbcdg.gov.in, linked from https://www.rrbapply.gov.in). No permanent official PYQ archive exists; memory-based papers from coaching publishers are unofficial.

questions.question: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 91 = 7 × 13, 87 = 3 × 29 and 93 = 3 × 31. 97 has no factor other than 1 and itself.

questions.question: Simplify: 3/4 of 2/5 of 1500 − 20% of 900
What is the least three-digit number which, when divided by 6, 8 and 12, leaves a remainder of 3 in each case?
questions.explanation: LCM(6, 8, 12) = 24. Numbers are of the form 24k + 3: 99 (two-digit), then 123. So the answer is 123.

questions.question: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, then A : B : C is:
questions.explanation: Make B common: A : B = 8 : 12 and B : C = 12 : 15. So A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.

questions.question: A number is first increased by 20% and then the result is decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid cylinder of radius 4 cm. What is the height of the cylinder?
The perimeter of a square is 48 cm. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Side = 48/4 = 12 cm. Area = 12² = 144 cm².

questions.topic: Square Root, Age, Calendar & Clock, Pipes & Cistern
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B can empty the full tank in 15 hours. If both are opened together on an empty tank, in how many hours will it be full?
questions.explanation: Net filling per hour = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. So the tank fills in 30 hours.

questions.question: A and B can do a work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can A alone do it?
A man travels from P to Q at 40 km/h and returns from Q to P at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2 × 40 × 60 / 100 = 48 km/h.

questions.question: At what rate of simple interest per annum will ₹2,500 amount to ₹3,100 in 4 years?
A sum of money doubles itself in 5 years at compound interest (compounded annually). In how many years will it become 8 times itself?
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, so it takes 3 doubling periods = 3 × 5 = 15 years.

questions.question: A dishonest shopkeeper sells goods at cost price but uses a weight of 900 g instead of 1 kg. What is his gain percentage?
questions.explanation: He gives 900 g for the price of 1000 g. Gain% = 100/900 × 100 = 11 1/9 %.

questions.question: If x − y = 4 and xy = 21, what is the value of x³ − y³?
The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
The mean of 5 observations is 12. If the observation 20 is removed, what is the mean of the remaining observations?
questions.explanation: Sum = 5 × 12 = 60. After removing 20, sum = 40 over 4 observations, mean = 10.

questions.question: Doctor : Hospital :: Teacher : ?
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital; a teacher works in a school (person : workplace).

questions.question: ACE : BDF :: GIK : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one step forward: A→B, C→D, E→F. Similarly G→H, I→J, K→L.

questions.question: Find the next number: 6, 11, 21, 41, 81, ?
questions.explanation: Each term = previous × 2 − 1: 81 × 2 − 1 = 161.

questions.question: Find the next letter: Z, W, S, N, ?
questions.explanation: Positions 26, 23, 19, 14 decrease by 3, 4, 5; next decrease is 6: 14 − 6 = 8 = H.

questions.question: Find the next number: 3, 4, 8, 17, 33, ?
questions.explanation: Differences are 1, 4, 9, 16 (squares); next difference is 25: 33 + 25 = 58.

questions.question: If RED is coded as 27 (sum of alphabet positions), what is the code for BLUE?
In a code language, 'sky is blue' is written 'ka ta pa', 'blue is deep' is written 'ta na ka' and 'deep sea' is written 'na ra'. What is the code for 'sky'?
questions.explanation: 'is' and 'blue' are common to the first two sentences, so they are 'ka' and 'ta'. The remaining word 'sky' must be 'pa'.

questions.question: A + B means A is the mother of B; A − B means A is the brother of B; A × B means A is the father of B; A ÷ B means A is the sister of B. Which expression shows that P is the maternal uncle of Q?
questions.explanation: P − M + Q: P is the brother of M and M is the mother of Q, so P is Q's maternal uncle. P − M × Q makes P a paternal uncle; P ÷ M + Q makes P a maternal aunt; P × M − Q makes P the father of Q.

questions.question: Introducing a woman, Aman (a man) said, 'She is the wife of my mother's only son.' How is the woman related to Aman?
questions.explanation: Aman is a man, so his mother's only son is Aman himself. The woman is his wife.

questions.question:
Statements: Some books are pens. All pens are pencils.
Conclusions: I. Some books are pencils. II. Some pencils are books.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The books that are pens are also pencils, so some books are pencils (I), and its conversion 'some pencils are books' (II) also follows.

questions.question:
Statements: All apples are fruits. No fruit is a vegetable.
Conclusions: I. No apple is a vegetable. II. Some vegetables are apples.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Apples lie inside fruits, which are completely separate from vegetables, so no apple is a vegetable (I). II contradicts I.

questions.question: Which set of classes is best represented by one circle lying completely inside a second circle, with a third circle completely separate from both?
questions.explanation: All roses are flowers (one circle inside the other) and a car is unrelated to both. Mammal–Dog–Cat has two circles inside one; India–Asia–World is a chain of three nested circles; Doctor–Male–Father overlap.

questions.question: Rahul walks 5 km south, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 9 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation: From (0, 0): south 5 → (0, −5); left of south is east, 3 → (3, −5); left of east is north, 9 → (3, 4). Distance = √(3² + 4²) = 5 km, towards the North-East.

questions.question: Select the odd one out: Triangle, Square, Circle, Rectangle
questions.explanation: Triangle, square and rectangle are polygons bounded by straight lines; a circle has no straight sides.

questions.question: M, N, O, P and Q sit in a row facing north. O sits at the extreme right end. M sits second to the left of O. N sits to the immediate left of Q. Who sits at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation: O = 5, so M = 3. N and Q must be adjacent with N on the left; only positions 1–2 are free together, so N = 1, Q = 2 and P = 4.

questions.question:
Statement: Should mobile phones be banned inside examination halls?
Arguments: I. Yes, they can be misused for cheating. II. No, almost everyone owns a mobile phone nowadays.
Which argument(s) are strong?
options: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: I gives a direct, relevant reason related to the fairness of the exam. II (wide ownership) is irrelevant to whether phones should be allowed in an exam hall.

questions.question: Arrange the words in dictionary order: 1. Govern 2. Gossip 3. Gold 4. Goal
questions.explanation: Comparing the third letters: Goal (a), Gold (l), Gossip (s), Govern (v). Order: 4, 3, 2, 1.

questions.question:
Question: Is the integer x even?
Statement I: x² is even.
Statement II: x is a multiple of 3.
Which statement(s) are sufficient to answer the question?
options: Both I and II together are needed
Neither I nor II is sufficient
questions.explanation: If x² is even, x must be even (the square of an odd number is odd), so I answers the question. A multiple of 3 can be odd (3) or even (6), so II alone does not.

questions.question:
Statement: Due to heavy rain, train services between two cities were cancelled for the day.
Conclusions: I. Heavy rain can disrupt train services. II. Trains never run during rain.
Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: The statement shows rain disrupted services (I). One cancellation does not mean trains never run in rain, so II is an over-generalisation.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: What is the SI unit of power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of doing work; 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A body moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest in 4 s by a uniform retardation. What is the magnitude of the retardation?
questions.explanation: a = (v − u)/t = (0 − 20)/4 = −5 m/s², so the retardation is 5 m/s².

questions.question: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r². Doubling r makes the force 1/2² = 1/4 of its original value.

questions.question: A crane lifts a load of 50 kg vertically through 10 m in 5 s. What is the power used? (g = 10 m/s²)
A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. What is its radius of curvature?
An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. At what distance from the lens is the image formed?
questions.explanation: Lens formula 1/v − 1/u = 1/f with u = −30, f = +20: 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm (real image on the other side).

questions.question: A potential difference of 5 V is applied across a 10 Ω resistor. What current flows through it?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law I = V/R = 5/10 = 0.5 A.

questions.question: A 1.5 kW heater is used for 2 hours every day. How much electrical energy does it consume in 30 days?
questions.explanation: Energy = 1.5 kW × 2 h × 30 = 90 kWh (90 units).

questions.question: Which device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
questions.explanation: A generator (dynamo) works on electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical energy to electrical energy; a motor does the reverse.

questions.question: In which of the following media does sound travel the fastest?
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids such as steel (≈5000 m/s), slower in water (≈1500 m/s), slower still in air (≈343 m/s), and cannot travel through vacuum.

questions.question: A sodium atom has atomic number 11 and mass number 23. How many neutrons does its nucleus contain?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 23 − 11 = 12.

questions.question: The Modern Periodic Table has:
questions.explanation: The long form of the Modern Periodic Table has 18 vertical columns (groups) and 7 horizontal rows (periods).

questions.question: The pH of human blood is about 7.4. This means blood is:
questions.explanation: pH 7 is neutral; values above 7 are basic. 7.4 is slightly basic (alkaline).

questions.question: Which of the following is the main ore of aluminium?
questions.explanation: Bauxite (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) is the ore of aluminium. Haematite is an iron ore, galena a lead ore and cinnabar a mercury ore.

questions.question: Deficiency of iodine in the diet causes:
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed to make thyroxine; its deficiency causes goitre. Anaemia is linked to iron, scurvy to vitamin C and rickets to vitamin D.

questions.question: The loss of water in the form of vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mainly through stomata, is called:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour through stomata. Guttation is loss of liquid water droplets; translocation is transport of food in phloem.

questions.question: Aditya-L1, launched by ISRO in September 2023, is India's first space-based mission to study:
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is a solar observatory placed in a halo orbit around Lagrange point L1 of the Sun–Earth system.

questions.question: Which team won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024?
questions.explanation: India beat South Africa by 7 runs in the final at Barbados on 29 June 2024.

questions.question: Who composed 'Vande Mataram', India's national song?
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram is from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel 'Anandamath' (1882). Tagore wrote the national anthem.

questions.question: The 'Make in India' initiative was launched by the Government of India in which year?
questions.explanation: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014 to promote manufacturing in India.

questions.question: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Article 324 the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President (on the recommendation of a selection committee under the 2023 Act).

questions.question: India's first passenger train, which ran on 16 April 1853, operated between:
questions.explanation: The first passenger train in India ran 34 km from Bori Bunder in Bombay to Thane on 16 April 1853.

questions.question: The Rail Coach Factory (RCF) of Indian Railways is located at:
questions.explanation: RCF is at Kapurthala (Punjab). Chennai has the Integral Coach Factory, Rae Bareli the Modern Coach Factory, and Varanasi the Banaras Locomotive Works.

questions.question: Before it was renamed in 2021, the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award was named after:
questions.explanation: India's highest sporting honour, earlier the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, was renamed after hockey legend Major Dhyan Chand in August 2021.

questions.question: If the six-digit number 52x638 is divisible by 9, what is the smallest possible value of the digit x?
questions.explanation: Sum of known digits = 5 + 2 + 6 + 3 + 8 = 24. For divisibility by 9, 24 + x must be a multiple of 9, so x = 3 (next would be 12, not a digit).

questions.question: What is the remainder when 2⁴⁰ is divided by 7?
Simplify: 3/5 of 4/7 of 1050 − 25% of 640
Two trains 180 m and 120 m long are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at 72 km/h and 54 km/h. How long will the faster train take to cross the slower train completely?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 72 − 54 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m. Time = 300/5 = 60 s. (Adding the speeds, as for opposite directions, gives about 8.6 s.)

questions.question: The recurring decimal 0.363636… expressed as a fraction in its lowest terms is:
What is the LCM of 2/3, 4/9 and 5/6?
questions.explanation: LCM of fractions = LCM of numerators ÷ HCF of denominators = LCM(2, 4, 5) ÷ HCF(3, 9, 6) = 20 ÷ 3 = 20/3.

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 4 : 5. Five years ago the ratio was 7 : 9. What is the present age of A?
The price of an article is first increased by 25% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change in its price?
questions.explanation: Net factor = 1.25 × 0.80 = 1.00, so the price is unchanged. (Formula: 25 − 20 − 25×20/100 = 0.)

questions.question: The total surface area of a cube is 294 cm². What is its volume?
questions.explanation: 6a² = 294 → a² = 49 → a = 7 cm. Volume = 7³ = 343 cm³.

questions.question: 18 workers working 8 hours a day can finish a job in 10 days. In how many days will 12 workers working 6 hours a day finish the same job?
A boat covers 30 km downstream in 2 hours and returns the same distance upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 15 km/h, upstream speed = 10 km/h. Stream speed = (15 − 10)/2 = 2.5 km/h.

questions.question: What is the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and the simple interest on ₹15,000 for 2 years at 8% per annum?
By selling a watch for ₹1,440 a shopkeeper gains 20%. What would be his gain or loss per cent if he sold it for ₹1,080?
If a + b = 9 and ab = 18, what is the value of a³ + b³?
If 5 tan θ = 4, what is the value of (5 sin θ − 3 cos θ)/(5 sin θ + 2 cos θ)?
questions.explanation: Divide numerator and denominator by cos θ: (5 tan θ − 3)/(5 tan θ + 2) = (4 − 3)/(4 + 2) = 1/6.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.
Odometer : Distance :: Anemometer : ?
questions.explanation: An odometer measures distance; an anemometer measures wind speed. Humidity, rainfall and pressure are measured by hygrometer, rain gauge and barometer.

questions.question:
Select the letter-cluster that is related to the third cluster in the same way as the second is related to the first.
CEG : HJL :: MOQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward: C→H, E→J, G→L. So M→R, O→T, Q→V = RTV.

questions.question:
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?
2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, ?

Find the wrong number in the following series.
4, 9, 19, 39, 79, 160
questions.explanation: Each term = previous × 2 + 1: 4→9→19→39→79→159. So 160 is wrong.

questions.question:
Which letter will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?
Z, X, U, Q, L, ?
In a certain code language, ROAD is written as URDG. How will SWAN be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted 3 places forward: R→U, O→R, A→D, D→G. So S→V, W→Z, A→D, N→Q = VZDQ.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'go home now' is written as 'ri ta mo', 'now come here' is written as 'mo li pa' and 'come home soon' is written as 'pa ta su'. What is the code for 'come'?
questions.explanation: 'now' is common to the first two sentences → mo. 'home' is common to the first and third → ta. 'come' is common to the second and third → pa.

questions.question:
If A stands for '×', B for '÷', C for '+' and D for '−', what is the value of the following?
64 B 8 A 5 C 12 D 9
If 7 * 3 = 58 and 5 * 4 = 41, then what is the value of 6 * 5?
Introducing a man, Sunita said, 'He is the son of the only brother of my mother.' How is the man related to Sunita?
questions.explanation: The only brother of Sunita's mother is her maternal uncle; his son is Sunita's cousin.

questions.question: 'P × Q' means P is the father of Q; 'P + Q' means P is the sister of Q; 'P − Q' means P is the brother of Q; 'P ÷ Q' means P is the mother of Q. If A ÷ B − C × D, how is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A is the mother of B; B is the brother of C, so A is also C's mother; C is the father of D. Hence A is D's father's mother – paternal grandmother.

questions.question:
Statements:
Some pens are pencils.
Some pencils are erasers.
Conclusions:
I. Some pens are erasers.
II. Some erasers are pencils.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
questions.explanation: Two "some" statements give no definite link between pens and erasers, so I does not follow. "Some pencils are erasers" converts to "Some erasers are pencils", so II follows. Only II.

questions.question:
Statements:
Some cups are plates.
No plate is a spoon.
Conclusions:
I. No cup is a spoon.
II. All spoons are cups.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s)?
questions.explanation: Cups that are plates cannot be spoons, but cups that are not plates may or may not be spoons, so I is not definite. Nothing supports II. Neither follows.

questions.question: In a group of 80 students, 45 study Hindi, 38 study Sanskrit and 12 study neither language. How many students study both languages?
questions.explanation: Students studying at least one = 80 − 12 = 68. Both = 45 + 38 − 68 = 15.

questions.question:
Question: What is the two-digit number N?
Statement I: The sum of the digits of N is 9.
Statement II: The tens digit of N is twice its units digit.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Statement I alone is sufficient, but Statement II alone is not
Statement II alone is sufficient, but Statement I alone is not
Even both statements together are not sufficient
questions.explanation: I alone allows 18, 27, 36, … ; II alone allows 21, 42, 63, 84. Together: t + u = 9 and t = 2u give u = 3, t = 6, so N = 63. Both statements are needed.

questions.question:
Statement: Because of a heavy festival rush, the railway has started a special train between two cities for one month.
Courses of action:
I. The railway should monitor the occupancy of the special train.
II. All regular trains on that route should be cancelled.
Which course(s) of action logically follow(s)?
questions.explanation: Monitoring occupancy helps decide whether the special service is needed – I follows. Cancelling regular trains would worsen the rush – II does not follow.

questions.question: Select the letter-cluster that is different from the others.
questions.explanation: In ACE, GIK and MOQ the letters move +2, +2. In RTW they move +2, +3, so RTW is the odd one.

questions.question: In a row of students, Amit is 12th from the left end and Sumit is 18th from the right end. When they interchange their positions, Amit becomes 25th from the left end. How many students are there in the row?
questions.explanation: After the swap Amit is at Sumit's old place, which is 25th from the left and 18th from the right. Total = 25 + 18 − 1 = 42.

questions.question: Six friends P, Q, R, S, T and U sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits opposite Q. R sits to the immediate left of P. S sits to the immediate right of Q. T is not an immediate neighbour of P. Who sits to the immediate right of P?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left = clockwise. Seats clockwise from P: P(1), R(2), S(3), Q(4), then 5 and 6. T cannot be next to P, so T = 5 and U = 6. The immediate right (anticlockwise neighbour) of P is U.

questions.question: From his house Raju drives 15 km south, then turns left and drives 8 km. How far and in which direction is he now from his house?
questions.explanation: Turning left while facing south means facing east. He is 15 km south and 8 km east of home: distance = √(15² + 8²) = 17 km, towards the South-East.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A car moving at 72 km/h is brought to rest by a uniform retardation in 5 s. What distance does it cover before stopping?
Which of the following substances is used by doctors for making casts to support fractured bones?
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O) mixed with water sets into a hard mass of gypsum, so it is used for plaster casts.

questions.topic: Physics: Units, Motion & Laws of Motion
questions.question: A bullet of mass 20 g is fired with a velocity of 400 m/s from a gun of mass 4 kg. What is the recoil velocity of the gun?
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: 0.02 × 400 = 4 × v → v = 8/4 = 2 m/s (opposite to the bullet).

questions.question: A body of mass 5 kg is raised to a height of 8 m above the ground. What is its potential energy? (g = 10 m/s²)
If the mass of one of two bodies is doubled and the distance between them is also doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
questions.explanation: F ∝ m₁m₂/r². New F = (2)/(2²) × F = F/2.

questions.question: What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm?
questions.explanation: P = 1/f (in metres) = 1/0.25 = +4 D. A convex lens has positive power.

questions.question: Hypermetropia (long-sightedness) is corrected by using:
questions.explanation: In hypermetropia the image of nearby objects forms behind the retina; a converging (convex) lens brings it onto the retina.

questions.question: Resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series across a 20 V battery. What current flows in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Series resistance = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 Ω. I = V/R = 20/10 = 2 A.

questions.question: What current is drawn by an 1100 W electric heater working on a 220 V supply?
A sound wave has a frequency of 500 Hz and a wavelength of 0.68 m. What is its speed?
When calcium carbonate is heated strongly, it forms calcium oxide and carbon dioxide (CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂). This is an example of:
questions.explanation: A single reactant breaks down into two simpler products on heating, so it is a (thermal) decomposition reaction.

questions.question: A colourless solution turns red litmus paper blue. Which of the following could be its pH?
questions.explanation: Red litmus turns blue in a basic solution, whose pH is greater than 7. Only 10 fits; 1 and 4 are acidic and 7 is neutral.

questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CHO?
questions.explanation: Three carbon atoms (prop-) with a terminal –CHO (aldehyde) group gives propanal. Propanone is CH₃COCH₃.

questions.question: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen gains oxygen to form H₂O, so H₂ is oxidised; CuO loses oxygen and is reduced.

questions.question: Which organ of the human body produces bile?
questions.explanation: Bile is produced by the liver and only stored in the gall bladder; it emulsifies fats in the small intestine.

questions.question: In human beings, the sex of the child is determined by:
options: The sex chromosome contributed by the father
The sex chromosome contributed by the mother
The blood groups of the parents
questions.explanation: The mother always gives an X chromosome; the father gives either X (girl) or Y (boy), so the father's contribution decides the sex.

questions.question: NISAR, the Earth-observation radar satellite launched in July 2025 from Sriharikota, is a joint mission of ISRO and:
questions.explanation: NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) was launched on 30 July 2025 aboard GSLV-F16.

questions.question: In 2025, which Indian Air Force officer became the first Indian to visit the International Space Station, flying on the Axiom-4 mission?
questions.explanation: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS on Axiom Mission 4 (launched 25 June 2025). Rakesh Sharma flew to the Salyut-7 station in 1984.

questions.question: Which team did India defeat in the final of the Men's Asia Cup cricket tournament 2025 held in the UAE?
questions.explanation: India beat Pakistan by five wickets in the final at Dubai on 28 September 2025.

questions.question: Divya Deshmukh won the FIDE Women's World Cup 2025 by defeating which fellow Indian player in the final?
questions.explanation: In the all-Indian final at Batumi (Georgia) in July 2025, Divya Deshmukh beat Koneru Humpy in the tie-breaks and also earned the Grandmaster title.

questions.question: The Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for Central Government employees came into effect from:
questions.explanation: Approved by the Union Cabinet in August 2024, the UPS became effective on 1 April 2025 as an option under the NPS.

questions.question: Who was sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India in November 2025?
questions.explanation: Justice Surya Kant took oath on 24 November 2025, succeeding Justice B. R. Gavai.

questions.question: Which is India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge, inaugurated in April 2025?
questions.explanation: The New Pamban Bridge links Rameswaram island to mainland Tamil Nadu; it was inaugurated on 6 April 2025.

questions.question: Which actor was announced in September 2025 as the recipient of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2023?
questions.explanation: Malayalam actor Mohanlal was named for the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India's highest honour in cinema, in September 2025.
